- When sentiment is negative (especially > -0.33), model tends to overcorrect upward; reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots and fails to correct; dampen next 3–5 periods by 3–7%.
- If recent history shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive declines), model overestimates recovery; lower forecast mid-range.
- When sentiment is positive but weak (0.11–0.17), model overreacts; cap upward bias at +5% of recent 7-day average.
- Model consistently overpredicts early in 30-day horizon; apply 2–4% downward adjustment for first 5–7 days.
- If sentiment history shows alternating +/– swings, model fails to capture volatility; smooth forecast with 3-period moving average.
